judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'MAPAS' item of the main navigation menu (#et-menu), linking to https://metsul.com/mapas/, whose page is titled 'Mapas meteorológicos' with heading 'MAPAS'. On a weather site the link text alone tells users it leads to the maps page. Every other link named MAPAS in the snapshot (secondary and mobile menus, all hidden) goes to the same address, so no shared-name pair exists under R1. The live HTML has the same menu link and the screenshot shows it in the visible header. The element meets 2.4.4, so this no-claim row is a false positive.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the search field in the dark-blue top header, placeholder 'Procurar'. The claim gives 1.61:1 (#324a69 on #274163), but the captured screenshot shows the placeholder as white uppercase 'PROCURAR' on a #1a4885 field. I sampled the screenshot pixels: #ffffff text on #1a4885, about 9.1:1. The live CSS agrees: '#et-info .et-top-search .et-search-field' sets color:#fff on a rgba(255,255,255,.1) background, and the theme's ::placeholder rule uses color:inherit. So the placeholder is white on blue, well over 4.5:1, and the claim is not true of the capture. The screenshot and the live page match each other. The colours in the snapshot's pixel-contrast record are the outlier: they gave the rule wrong data. The element meets 1.4.3.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the USERNAME field (input type=text name=log) of the visible 'ACESSO ASSINANTE' subscriber login widget in the sidebar. Its only name is the placeholder, and it has no autocomplete attribute, in the snapshot and in the live HTML alike (the live page has no autocomplete attribute anywhere). It collects the user's own username, a purpose listed in WCAG 2.1 section 7 ('username - A username'). Without autocomplete="username" (technique H98), that purpose cannot be programmatically determined, so the field fails 1.3.5, as the claim says.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Geral' category pill above the article headline (title='Geral', in a div aria-label='Categorias' beside Paraná, Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina). It links to https://metsul.com/categoria/geral/, whose heading is 'Geral'. The link text is the name of the section it opens, which Understanding 2.4.4 accepts as describing the purpose. No other link shares the name, so R1 does not apply. The live HTML has the same four pills, matching the snapshot and screenshot. The element meets 2.4.4, so this no-claim row is a false positive.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Entrar no canal' button-styled link in the WhatsApp call-to-action box, linking to a WhatsApp channel. The text alone does not say which channel, but the heading just before it in document order is the h3 'Siga a MetSul no WhatsApp' (context under the rubric, H80). Together they give the purpose: join MetSul's WhatsApp channel. The destination's og:title is 'Metsul Meteorologia', which confirms it. It is the only link with that name. The live HTML and screenshot match the snapshot. The element meets 2.4.4, so this no-claim row is a false positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the SENHA field (input type=password name=pwd) of the visible sidebar subscriber login form, which posts to wp-login.php. It has no autocomplete attribute, in the snapshot and in the live HTML alike. It collects the user's current password for logging in, a purpose listed in WCAG 2.1 section 7 ('current-password - The current password for the account identified by the username field (e.g., when logging in)'). Without autocomplete="current-password", that purpose is not programmatically determined, so the field fails 1.3.5, as the claim says.
